hero.headline: US proposes new funding rules allowing grant cancellations at any time
hero.body:
The US government proposed new funding rules that would allow officials to cancel research grants at any time, according to documents released Friday. The proposal also makes peer review optional for grant decisions.

Under the proposed changes, political staff would screen grant applications for topics the administration considers forbidden. The rules represent a significant shift from current research funding practices, where grants typically undergo peer review by independent scientists and maintain guaranteed funding periods once awarded.

The proposal comes as federal research agencies distribute billions of dollars annually to universities, hospitals, and research institutions across the country. These grants support scientific work ranging from basic research to clinical trials.

Peer review has served as the standard process for evaluating grant applications at agencies like the National Institutes of Health and National Science Foundation for decades. Scientists submit proposals that undergo assessment by other researchers in their field, who evaluate the work's merit without political considerations.

The new rules would fundamentally alter this system. Making peer review optional would allow agency leadership to approve or reject grants without independent scientific assessment. The ability to cancel grants at any time would eliminate the funding stability researchers currently rely on for multi-year projects.

The proposal does not specify which topics would be considered forbidden or who would make those determinations. It also leaves unclear whether existing grants could face retroactive cancellation or if the rules would apply only to new awards.

Research institutions depend on federal grants to fund laboratory operations, pay graduate students and postdoctoral researchers, and purchase equipment. Sudden cancellations could force labs to shut down experiments mid-stream and dismiss staff.

The proposed rules remain subject to a public comment period before any final implementation. Federal agencies have not announced a timeline for when the changes might take effect or provided estimates of how many grants could be affected.

cards.headline: Trump delays decision on proposed US-Iran agreement
cards.body:
President Trump has postponed making a final decision on a draft peace agreement with Iran after circulating it among allies including Israel. The delay comes as both sides work to prevent ceasefire violations from derailing negotiations.

Trump indicated he needed additional time to consider the proposal rather than discuss it during a Wednesday cabinet meeting. Vice President JD Vance said on Thursday that the US and Iran were close to reaching a deal, but disagreements remained on specific points.

"It's hard to say exactly when or if the president is going to sign the memorandum of understanding. We're going back and forth on a couple of language points," Vance said, referring to unresolved issues around Iran's enriched uranium stockpile and its enrichment programme.

The draft agreement circulating in the region outlines several key provisions. The Strait of Hormuz would be reopened to commercial shipping within 30 days, the US blockade on Iranian ports would be lifted, and Iran would gain access to approximately $12 billion in frozen assets. Negotiations over Iran's nuclear programme, including discussions about its uranium stockpile and International Atomic Energy Agency supervision, would continue for up to 60 days. Iran would renounce the use of nuclear weapons.

Despite these terms, significant obstacles remain. Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, expressed internal political concerns about negotiations, telling officials not to allow disagreements to create divisions and to address public economic worries.

The ceasefire itself remains fragile. On Thursday, Iran targeted a US airbase in Kuwait in response to what Washington described as a strike against an Iranian drone operation near the strait. The Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps' navy has reasserted control over the waterway, requiring permission for commercial vessels to pass and preventing ships sailing with transponders off from transiting.

International mediation efforts continue. Pakistan's foreign minister, Mohammad Ishaq Dar, is scheduled to visit Washington on Friday to meet with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in an attempt to accelerate negotiations.

A significant source of tension involves access to the strait. Iran has attempted to negotiate a separate agreement with Oman that would impose fees for navigational services. Trump threatened on Wednesday to "blow up" Oman if it pursued such an arrangement, prompting the US Treasury Secretary to threaten sanctions against any countries involved in establishing toll systems.

Israel views the current draft as problematic because it defers Iran's firm nuclear commitments and requires a permanent ceasefire that includes Lebanon. China is pressing for UN Security Council ratification of any agreement.

Oil prices climbed 2 percent Thursday morning following reports of the potential breakthrough but remained below $100 a barrel. The uncertainty surrounding Trump's approval has left the agreement's implementation timeline unclear.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Drop as US and Iran Move Toward Agreement
cards.teaser: Oil markets declined and stocks fluctuated as investors reacted to signs of progress toward a US-Iran pact extending a cease-fire.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell on Thursday following reports of a potential breakthrough in US-Iran talks. The tentative agreement, which would extend a ceasefire between the two nations, is subject to Donald Trump's approval.

The developments come as US inflation has risen at its fastest pace in three years, driven in part by higher energy prices from the ongoing conflict with Iran. The surge in costs has eroded household purchasing power and frustrated Americans with the administration's economic management ahead of the midterms.

cards.headline: SEC Proposes Repeal of Climate Disclosure Rule for Companies
cards.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission moved to repeal a rule requiring companies to report greenhouse gas emissions and climate risks. The agency proposed scrapping the Biden-era regulation that mandated climate change disclosures from publicly traded firms.

The rule had required companies to include information about their carbon emissions and how climate change might affect their business operations in regulatory filings. The proposed repeal represents a reversal of the previous administration's policy on corporate environmental transparency.

The SEC's action aligns with broader regulatory changes under the current administration. Wall Street's top regulator is now seeking to eliminate requirements that companies assess and disclose climate-related financial risks to investors.

The original climate disclosure rule was part of efforts to give investors more information about how environmental factors might impact company performance and valuations. Supporters argued the requirements helped shareholders make informed decisions about climate-related business risks.

The proposed repeal must go through a formal regulatory process before taking effect. The SEC will likely accept public comments on the proposal before making a final decision on whether to eliminate the reporting requirements.

Companies that had begun preparing climate disclosures under the rule now face uncertainty about future reporting obligations. The rule had affected publicly traded corporations across industries, from energy companies to financial institutions.

The move follows other regulatory rollbacks affecting environmental and corporate governance policies. Several Biden-era rules addressing climate and sustainability issues have faced revision or elimination under the new administration.

cards.headline: European Union to Release Billions to Hungary After Orban Defeat
cards.teaser: The EU is set to release 16 billion euros it had withheld as Hungary moves to enact anti-corruption policies.
cards.body:
The European Union will release more than €16 billion to Hungary that had been frozen during Viktor Orbán's tenure as prime minister. EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described the decision as reflecting "winds of change" following the election of new Prime Minister Péter Magyar last month.

The breakthrough comes alongside a significant policy shift on civil liberties. Hungarian police have announced they will permit next month's Pride parade in Budapest to proceed—a reversal from the previous government's attempt to block the event.

cards.headline: Ghana Parliament Approves Anti-LGBTQ Bill
cards.teaser: Same-sex acts are punishable by jail terms under the new legislation targeting gay, lesbian, and transgender individuals.
cards.body:
Ghana's parliament has passed legislation that criminalizes same-sex acts and targets individuals who identify as gay, lesbian, or transgender. Under the new bill, those engaging in such acts face jail sentences.

The measure marks a major setback for LGBTQ rights in the West African nation. Human rights advocates have condemned the bill as a violation of fundamental freedoms, while parliamentary supporters maintain it aligns with cultural and religious values held by many Ghanaians.

cards.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes During Test at Florida Launch Site
cards.teaser: A Blue Origin rocket exploded during testing at Cape Canaveral, causing damage to the launch complex and sending space industry stocks lower.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a hotfire test at Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Thursday night at 9pm ET. The blast destroyed the launch pad at Cape Canaveral, creating a massive fireball visible as an orange sky from Fort Pierce, 115 miles away. Blue Origin stated that no personnel were harmed and referred to the incident as an anomaly.

The explosion threatens NASA's lunar plans, which depend on New Glenn for a lunar base and crewed moon missions scheduled within two years. The incident represents another setback for the Jeff Bezos-owned company.

hero.headline: Russian Drone Strikes Apartment Building in Romania, Injuring Civilians
hero.body:
A Russian drone struck an apartment building in the Romanian city of Galati on Friday, injuring two people in what officials confirmed as the first such attack on Romanian soil to cause injuries. Romania is a NATO member state.

The drone hit the residential building during an overnight Russian assault on neighboring Ukraine. The impact ignited a fire on the building's roof and forced the evacuation of several residents. Emergency services responded to the scene, and police confirmed the two injuries.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte responded swiftly to the incident. "Russia's reckless behaviour is a danger to us all," Rutte wrote on social media following a call with Romanian President Nicuşor Dan. He affirmed that "NATO stands ready to defend every inch of allied territory."

Romanian officials took immediate action. President Dan convened an emergency meeting of the country's supreme council of national defence on Friday. The foreign ministry summoned Russia's ambassador and described the incident as a "grave and irresponsible escalation" and serious breach of international law.

Romanian Foreign Minister Oana Țoiu stated on social media that Romania would "officially communicate the consequences that this lack of responsibility on the part of the Russian Federation will have for the diplomatic relations between our countries, as well as the next steps at the European level regarding sanctions packages."

The foreign ministry requested that NATO accelerate the transfer of anti-drone capabilities to Romania. Officials also suggested the country would invoke Article 4 of the NATO treaty, which triggers formal discussions within the alliance about threats to a member state's security.

The Romanian military scrambled two F-16 fighter jets and a helicopter authorized to engage targets in response to the incident. The defense ministry said the drone was tracked by radar in Romanian airspace before crashing into the residential building in Galati, which sits on the Danube River west of the borders with Moldova and Ukraine.

President Dan stated that Romania would not accept the war being transferred to its citizens and instructed the foreign ministry to prepare a package of measures regarding Romania's relationship with Moscow that would be "proportionate to this very serious situation."

Russian President Vladimir Putin disputed responsibility for the incident, suggesting without evidence that the drone might have been a stray Ukrainian weapon. He told reporters he had only recently learned of the incident and requested that drone wreckage be handed over to Russia for an independent investigation.

The incident prompted condemnation from European leaders. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot denounced Russia's "irresponsible act," while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Russia's "war of aggression has crossed yet another line" and pledged European solidarity with Romania.

Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha characterized the incident as evidence that Russian aggression poses a threat to all of Europe and the broader region.

cards.headline: Trump Delays Decision on Iran Cease-Fire Proposal
cards.teaser: The president met with aides for two hours at the White House about a possible cease-fire extension.
cards.body:
President Trump met with advisers for two hours at the White House to discuss a potential cease-fire extension with Iran. A senior administration official confirmed the meeting took place, though no announcement followed the discussions.

The US and Iran had previously agreed on a framework for a deal. However, Trump postponed making a final determination on the proposal despite earlier suggesting he was ready to do so.

cards.headline: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty to Aiding 14 Suicides
cards.teaser: Kenneth Law admitted charges relating to Canadian victims after selling toxic chemicals online to people worldwide.
cards.body:
A Canadian man has pleaded guilty to 14 counts of assisting suicide after selling lethal chemicals online to people worldwide. Kenneth Law appeared in an Ontario courtroom where prosecutors withdrew 14 murder charges in exchange for his guilty plea. He mailed "suicide packets" containing poison and instructions to more than 100 people across multiple countries, including Canada, the UK, the US, Italy, Australia, and New Zealand.

Families of victims in Britain have called for Law to face additional charges there, where 79 deaths have been linked to his activities. His sentencing is scheduled for September.

cards.headline: Trump's Boat Strikes Fail to Reduce Cocaine Flow to US
cards.teaser: Despite a rising body count off South America, cocaine remains as available in the US as before the strikes began.
cards.body:
Military operations targeting drug trafficking vessels off South America's coast have not decreased cocaine availability throughout the United States, according to researchers. Despite mounting casualties from these strikes, the drug remains as accessible in many American communities as it was before the operations commenced.

The enforcement approach has failed to disrupt the underlying supply chains feeding cocaine into the country. Experts conclude the strategy has not achieved its primary objective, raising questions about the effectiveness of the military intervention despite its significant human toll.

cards.headline: Former Attorney General Bondi Defends Epstein Files Handling
cards.teaser: Pam Bondi testified about her management of the case roughly a month after being removed by President Trump.
cards.body:
Former US Attorney General Pam Bondi testified before Congress regarding her handling of files related to Jeffrey Epstein. The congressional probe examined how Bondi managed the Epstein case materials during her tenure as the nation's top prosecutor.

Bondi's testimony occurred approximately one month after President Donald Trump removed her from the position of attorney general. She previously served as Florida's attorney general before being appointed to lead the Justice Department.

cards.headline: Death toll reaches nine in Longview paper mill disaster
cards.teaser: Authorities confirmed a ninth fatality following the chemical tank rupture at a Nippon paper mill in Longview.
cards.body:
Crews recovered the remains of a ninth victim from the chemical tank rupture at a Nippon paper mill in Longview, Washington. Two workers remain unaccounted for following the disaster.

Among those killed were two brothers who worked together at the mill, along with other employees including a trivia champion and an electrician known for helping farmer neighbors with hay cutting. Families have identified some of the victims.

cards.headline: Bus collision kills five in Virginia
cards.teaser: A bus struck multiple cars in Virginia, killing five people and injuring 34 others, state police reported.
cards.body:
A bus collision in Virginia left five people dead and 34 injured, according to state police. The bus struck multiple cars during the incident.

State police confirmed the casualty figures and said the injured were receiving medical treatment. The collision involved the bus and several passenger vehicles on a Virginia roadway.

cards.headline: Former Attorney General Bondi testifies in Epstein files investigation
cards.teaser: Pam Bondi appeared before lawmakers and shifted responsibility for the release of Epstein files to Todd Blanche.
cards.body:
Former Attorney General Pam Bondi testified before Congress about her handling of Epstein files. During the hearing, she distanced herself from decisions regarding the files and shifted responsibility to Todd Blanche. Her testimony came approximately one month after she was ousted by President Donald Trump.

Democrats used the proceedings to scrutinize Bondi's role in the matter and signaled plans to focus their investigation on Blanche next.

cards.headline: Judge blocks Trump attempt to rename Kennedy Center
cards.teaser: A federal judge ordered the president's name removed from the Kennedy Center memorial and blocked efforts to close the facility.
cards.body:
A federal judge ordered President Trump's name removed from the Kennedy Center, ruling that the performing arts venue must remain named after the late President John F. Kennedy. In a 94-page decision, the judge determined it was "crystal clear" that the center's identity was tied to the Kennedy legacy.

The ruling also blocked Trump's plan to close the facility for two years of renovations. Following the court decision, Trump stated he had no interest in the Kennedy Center and announced plans to transfer it to Congress.

cards.headline: Three ICE protesters convicted of conspiracy in Spokane
cards.teaser: A federal jury found three people guilty of conspiracy for their participation in a protest at an ICE facility in downtown Spokane.
cards.body:
A federal jury has convicted three protesters, including a US military veteran, of felony conspiracy charges for their participation in a June 2025 protest against an Immigration and Customs Enforcement facility in Spokane, Washington. The defendants now face potential sentences of up to six years in prison and $250,000 in fines.

Legal experts say the case represents a significant escalation in the Trump administration's prosecution strategy against protesters and raises concerns about first amendment rights. Spokane's mayor criticized the verdict.

cards.headline: Airlines warn against restricting international flights to Newark
cards.teaser: Airlines and business groups cautioned that pulling customs officers from Newark airport could cause travel chaos.
cards.body:
Acting Customs Commissioner Mullin is considering pulling customs officers from Newark airport as part of an effort to pressure sanctuary jurisdictions. Airlines and business groups warned the move would create chaos for international travelers.

The plan targets airports in areas Mullin has labeled sanctuary cities. Airlines urged the Trump administration not to curb international flights in the dispute. Questions remain about whether immigration enforcement will be affected at other major venues including World Cup sites.

cards.headline: Salmonella Outbreak Linked to Moringa Supplements Sold Through Major Retailers
cards.teaser: Health officials linked a salmonella outbreak to moringa capsules sold through Amazon, Walmart, and Target, prompting a recall of the supplements.
cards.body:
The CDC identified moringa capsules as the source of a multistate salmonella outbreak affecting residents in eastern and western Washington. The contaminated supplements were sold through Amazon, Walmart, Target, and TikTok Shop.

The FDA recalled the affected products as health authorities worked to remove them from store shelves and investigate the full scope of the outbreak.

cards.teaser: Oil markets declined and stocks fluctuated as investors reacted to signs of progress toward a US-Iran pact extending a cease-fire.

The developments come as US inflation has risen at its fastest pace in three years, driven in part by higher energy prices from the ongoing conflict with Iran. The surge in costs has eroded household purchasing power and frustrated Americans with the administration's economic management ahead of the midterms.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Close at Records with S&P 500 Extending Winning Streak
cards.teaser: Major stock indexes reached new closing highs, with the S&P 500 posting its ninth consecutive weekly gain as technology stocks led the rally.
cards.body:
The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all finished at record highs, closing out a successful month for investors. Technology stocks, particularly Dell, drove the broader market rally higher. The S&P 500 extended its winning streak to nine consecutive weeks.

The Nasdaq climbed eight percent in May as artificial intelligence and technology stocks continued their strong performance. Wall Street ended the month with fresh records as optimism around the tech sector remained high.

cards.headline: Universal Music Group Rejects Bill Ackman's $64 Billion Takeover Bid
cards.teaser: The music company turned down a takeover proposal from billionaire Bill Ackman's Pershing Square, saying the offer undervalued the business.
cards.body:
Universal Music Group has rejected a $64 billion takeover proposal from Bill Ackman's Pershing Square investment firm. The company's board determined that the bid fundamentally and materially undervalued the business.

The music giant, which owns rights to recordings from major artists, declined the offer after reviewing its terms. Pershing Square's proposal represented one of the largest potential acquisitions in the music industry.

cards.headline: Train Fire at Penn Station Injures Five and Disrupts Commuter Service
cards.teaser: A maintenance train caught fire near Penn Station during rush hour, injuring five people and causing delays for Amtrak, LIRR, and NJ Transit passengers.
cards.body:
A fire broke out on an Amtrak maintenance train near Penn Station during evening rush hour, injuring five people. The incident disrupted service for commuters relying on the Long Island Rail Road and NJ Transit, causing delays of up to 60 minutes.

The fire highlighted ongoing infrastructure challenges at Penn Station, a major transit hub serving the New York metropolitan area. The MTA identified Amtrak tunnel repairs as a persistent problem contributing to service disruptions at the station.

cards.headline: SpaceX receives $6.45 billion in Space Force contracts before IPO
cards.teaser: The contracts add to SpaceX's government revenue stream as the company prepares to go public.
cards.body:
SpaceX received $6.45 billion in contracts from the Space Force, the company announced Friday. These awards arrive as SpaceX prepares for its initial public offering.

The company disclosed in its IPO filing that government contracts already accounted for one-fifth of its 2025 revenue. The new Space Force agreements will expand SpaceX's reliance on federal contracts going forward.

cards.headline: Court blocks US plan to send Ebola-exposed Americans to Kenya
cards.teaser: A Kenyan court stopped the Trump administration from transferring Americans exposed to Ebola to the country.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court blocked the Trump administration's plan to send Americans exposed to Ebola to Kenya for quarantine and treatment. The ruling came after the White House announced it was building a dedicated facility in Kenya for Americans who had been exposed to Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Some health experts have criticized the approach, arguing that preventing exposed Americans from returning to the US could hinder treatment efforts. The US already operates specialized facilities designed for treating Ebola patients and quarantining exposed individuals.

cards.headline: Botnet controlling over 17 million devices taken down
cards.teaser: Law enforcement dismantled a massive botnet reportedly linked to a Russian proxy network.
cards.body:
Authorities dismantled a botnet that controlled more than 17 million devices, according to announcements made Friday. The operation represents one of the largest botnet takedowns on record.

The botnet was reportedly connected to a Russia-based residential proxy network. These networks route internet traffic through compromised home devices, allowing operators to mask their locations and identities while conducting online activity.

cards.headline: Indian court ruling on Google ads draws founder criticism
cards.teaser: A court decision about Google's advertising business prompted renewed criticism from company founders.
cards.body:
An Indian court ruling on Google's advertising practices has drawn criticism of the search giant's business model from company founders. The decision centers on how Google manages ads that bid on trademarked terms, and lawyers suggest it could require platforms to change their approach to handling such keywords in advertising.

Founders have used the ruling to revive longstanding complaints about Google's ad operations. The decision may force platforms to reconsider their trademarked keyword advertising practices.

cards.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft tease new N1X laptop processors
cards.teaser: Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm posted coordinated messages hinting at new laptop chip announcements.
cards.body:
Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm are teasing the upcoming announcement of Nvidia's N1X laptop processors through coordinated social media posts. Both the Windows and Nvidia GeForce accounts posted "A new era of PC" on X, with Arm following suit with similar messaging.

The announcements precede Computex this weekend, where Nvidia is expected to officially unveil the new Arm-powered chips. Microsoft has also teased new Surface hardware, with the company's Surface chief hinting at something coming for developers, accompanied by an image suggesting a curved display design.

cards.headline: Developers increasingly refuse to code without AI tools
cards.teaser: Programmers are turning down work that does not allow AI coding assistants, raising concerns about code quality.
cards.body:
Software developers are increasingly rejecting job offers that don't allow AI coding tools, according to researchers. The tools enable programmers to write code more quickly and in greater volumes than before.

However, researchers caution that speed doesn't guarantee quality. The long-term effects of relying on AI-generated code remain uncertain, and development teams may face unforeseen problems as a result of this approach.

hero.headline: Pentagon recruits troops to attend White House UFC event
hero.body:
The Pentagon has circulated internal memos recruiting military personnel to attend UFC fights at the White House, according to documents obtained by The Washington Post. The events are being held to mark President Trump's birthday.

Troops seeking free tickets to the White House UFC event must meet specific weight standards, according to CNN. NBC News reported that attendees must meet fitness criteria, though no heavyweight fighters are allowed to participate.

The recruitment effort represents an intersection between the military and mixed martial arts at the presidential residence. Time Magazine traced how UFC president Dana White built the organization from a fringe sport into an enterprise that now hosts events at the White House.

The UFC has grown significantly under White's leadership over the past two decades. The organization previously faced criticism and regulatory challenges but has since become a mainstream sports property with broadcast deals and international events.

White has maintained a close relationship with Trump dating back years before the presidency. The UFC president has appeared at political rallies and campaign events supporting Trump.

The White House UFC event marks an unusual use of the presidential residence for a professional sporting competition. Previous administrations have hosted championship teams and individual athletes, but staging active competitive fights at the White House breaks with typical protocol.

Vox reported on the political dimensions of hosting the UFC event for Trump's birthday. The recruitment of active-duty military personnel to attend raises questions about the use of Defense Department resources for what critics characterize as a political celebration.

The weight and fitness requirements for troop attendance remain detailed in the Pentagon memos. Military personnel interested in attending must demonstrate they meet service fitness standards to qualify for the free tickets being distributed through official channels.

Trump has also indicated his attendance at other high-profile events. He stated he will attend the White House Correspondents' Association dinner for the first time as president, saying it will be "the GREATEST, HOTTEST, and MOST SPECTACULAR DINNER, OF ANY KIND, EVER." The White House Correspondents' Association has invited mentalist Oz Pearlman to entertain guests rather than a comedian.

Since Trump's return to the presidency in 2025, his allies have acquired major media companies, including David Ellison's purchase of Paramount, the parent company of CBS News. Last week, Paramount made a successful bid to acquire Warner Bros Discovery, which operates CNN.

The administration is also pursuing other initiatives to mark the nation's 250th anniversary. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the White House is pushing Congress to approve a $250 bill bearing Trump's portrait, which would require changing longstanding federal law that prohibits any living person from appearing on US currency. Bessent said the treasury has already started preparing for the possibility of the new currency.

cards.headline: Washington Nationals fire executive after hidden-camera video
cards.teaser: The baseball team dismissed an official following the release of a video showing comments about avoiding conservative players on social media.
cards.body:
The Washington Nationals dismissed a team executive following the release of a hidden-camera video containing comments about the organization's social media strategy. According to the recording, the executive indicated the team avoided featuring a conservative player in its social media content.

The incident has drawn scrutiny from federal authorities. The Department of Justice is reportedly investigating allegations of religious discrimination, with sources identifying the player involved as a Catholic pitcher. The executive's recorded remarks allegedly acknowledged the team's discriminatory practices based on religious affiliation.

cards.headline: Joao Fonseca upsets Novak Djokovic at French Open
cards.teaser: The 19-year-old Brazilian defeated the 39-year-old tennis champion in a third-round match at Roland Garros.
cards.body:
Brazilian teenager João Fonseca staged a remarkable comeback to defeat Novak Djokovic 4-6, 4-6, 6-3, 7-5, 7-5 in a five-set epic at Roland Garros. After Djokovic established a commanding two-set lead on Court Philippe-Chatrier, the 19-year-old gradually worked his way back into the match, ultimately prevailing in a grueling four-hour contest.

The victory blocks the 39-year-old Djokovic's path to claiming a 25th Grand Slam title. Fonseca's triumph represents a significant coming-of-age moment for the rising star, announcing his arrival among tennis's elite competitors and continuing a trend of top seeds falling at this year's French Open.

cards.headline: Giants players Abdul Carter and Jaxson Dart address Trump disagreement
cards.teaser: Two New York Giants players spoke publicly after Carter criticized quarterback Dart for appearing at a political rally.
cards.body:
Giants defensive end Abdul Carter publicly called out teammate quarterback Jaxson Dart following Dart's introduction of President Trump at a campaign rally. Carter's remarks signaled his own opposition to Trump's candidacy.

Following their initial disagreement, Carter and Dart expressed unity, according to ESPN. Both players discussed the situation regarding Dart's rally appearance.

cards.headline: Milwaukee upsets Auburn in NCAA baseball tournament opener
cards.teaser: The University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee defeated fourth-ranked Auburn in the first round of the NCAA tournament.
cards.body:
Milwaukee shocked Auburn in an NCAA tournament baseball game, eliminating the fourth-seeded Tigers from the regional competition. The upset victory came in Milwaukee's opening game against the heavily favored Auburn squad.

The result received significant local attention in Wisconsin, with WISN reporting the win as major news ahead of a Milwaukee Brewers game. Auburn had entered the tournament as one of the top-ranked teams in college baseball, making the first-round elimination an unexpected outcome for the program.

cards.headline: Sacramento makes pitch for MLB expansion team
cards.teaser: California city officials presented a proposal to bring a Major League Baseball franchise to the Sacramento area.
cards.body:
Sacramento leaders made a formal pitch to Major League Baseball for an expansion team to be located in West Sacramento. KCRA reported local fans expressed readiness for a professional baseball franchise in the region.

The Sacramento Bee identified several prominent investors already involved in the expansion effort, while others have withdrawn from consideration. Deseret News noted that Sacramento represents another Western city pursuing MLB expansion, joining other markets seeking to add teams to the league.

cards.headline: NCAA baseball tournament regionals begin
cards.teaser: The 2026 Men's College World Series regional rounds started with games across multiple sites.
cards.body:
The NCAA baseball tournament began its regional competition, with ESPN previewing matchups and top players to watch. USA Today provided the bracket, scores and television schedule for the opening weekend of games.

Yahoo Sports highlighted several storylines entering the tournament, including whether UCLA can advance deep into the competition and if the Southeastern Conference will claim another national championship. NCAA.com published the complete bracket and schedule for the path to the College World Series.

hero.headline: Marcia Lucas, Oscar-Winning Star Wars Editor, Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the film editor who won an Oscar for her work on Star Wars, died Wednesday in Rancho Mirage, California. She was 80. The family's attorney confirmed she died of cancer.

Lucas was a prominent film editor during the 1970s, shaping several influential films of that era. She won an Academy Award for editing Star Wars, which was directed by her former husband George Lucas. Her editing work helped define the final cut of one of the most successful films in cinema history.

Beyond Star Wars, Lucas edited American Graffiti and contributed to other notable productions during a decade that transformed American filmmaking. Her work during this period established her as a significant figure in the industry.

The family's attorney described her as a brilliant storyteller and a trailblazer in film editing. Her contributions to Star Wars extended beyond technical editing to shaping the narrative structure that made the film resonate with audiences worldwide.

Lucas was married to George Lucas during the production of his early films, including American Graffiti and Star Wars. The couple later divorced, but her professional achievements stood independently as a major force in 1970s cinema.

She retired from film editing after her Oscar-winning work, stepping away from Hollywood at the height of her career. Lucas spent her later years in California, away from the film industry that she had helped reshape through her editing choices.

Her death removes one of the last remaining major creative forces behind the original Star Wars film. The movie, released in 1977, transformed both the science fiction genre and the broader film industry, with Lucas's editing playing a central role in its storytelling success.

cards.headline: Over Half of Great American State Fair Performers Cancel Shows Amid Political Backlash
cards.teaser: More than half of the scheduled performers have dropped out of a Trump-backed concert planned for America's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
Artists have been canceling appearances at the Trump-linked Freedom 250 concert series planned for America's 250th anniversary celebration. Martina McBride and Morris Day are among the performers who have withdrawn from the event.

The cancellations come amid what sources describe as political controversy and threats related to the concerts. The Great American State Fair concerts were organized as part of the Freedom 250 events, which are separate from the official America250 anniversary planning efforts.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Rest of 2026 Concert Schedule for Health Reasons
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old singer announced he is canceling all remaining shows this year to focus on his health.
cards.body:
The 92-year-old singer announced Friday that he is canceling his remaining 2026 concert dates to focus on his health. Valli shared the news on social media and expressed his regret about disappointing fans who had purchased tickets for the shows.

Despite his age, Valli has maintained an active touring schedule throughout his long career in music.

cards.headline: Erika Kirk Denies Reports She Has New Boyfriend After Charlie Kirk's Death
cards.teaser: The widow of Charlie Kirk responded to rumors that she is dating again, less than a year after her husband's assassination.
cards.body:
Erika Kirk addressed rumors that she has a new boyfriend following the assassination of her husband Charlie Kirk. She denied the claims in a public statement, saying her late husband's love will last her a lifetime.

Charlie Kirk was killed less than a year ago. Erika Kirk told those spreading the rumors to go touch grass, pushing back against speculation about her personal life in the months following her husband's death.

cards.headline: A24's Backrooms Film Earns Over $10 Million in Previews
cards.teaser: The horror film directed by 20-year-old Kane Parsons has already earned more than $10 million before its nationwide release.
cards.body:
Backrooms, the directorial debut of 20-year-old Kane Parsons, has already grossed more than $10 million during preview screenings. The A24 horror film is now playing in theaters nationwide and is expected to perform strongly at the box office.

The film draws inspiration from the original Backrooms YouTube series, which became a viral internet phenomenon. Parsons' adaptation brings the eerie concept to the big screen as the filmmaker's first feature film.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Councilwoman Calls for Uncapped Film Tax Credits
cards.teaser: Nithya Raman urged California governor candidates to support unlimited tax incentives for film and television production.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Councilwoman Nithya Raman urged candidates for governor to support uncapped tax incentives for film and television production in the final days before the Tuesday election. Raman appeared outside Radford Studios with entertainment figures including Mike Schur, Cord Jefferson, and Kay Cannon.

Raman said California must ensure that Hollywood remains competitive for production work. The councilwoman, who is running for mayor, made the appeal with support from entertainment industry professionals who back her mayoral campaign.

cards.headline: Kanye West Approved to Perform in the Netherlands
cards.teaser: Officials ruled there was insufficient evidence to ban the rapper from entering the country for a birthday performance.
cards.body:
Dutch officials ruled that Kanye West can perform in the Netherlands on his birthday. Authorities determined that insufficient evidence existed to ban the rapper from entering the country.

The decision clears the way for West to hold the scheduled performance. Officials had considered whether to prevent his entry but found no basis to do so.

hero.headline: Judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
hero.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C. ordered President Trump to remove his name from the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. The ruling, signed Friday by a district judge, gives the president two weeks to remove his name from the building and surrounding signage.

The decision halts Trump's planned renovation of the performing arts venue, which was scheduled to close later this year so construction work could begin. The judge concluded that the Kennedy Center's board overstepped its legal authority by unilaterally agreeing to the name change and renovation plans.

The Kennedy Center operates as a federally chartered nonprofit institution and serves as the national cultural center. The facility hosts theatrical performances, concerts, and other cultural events in the nation's capital.

The court order represents a setback to the president's efforts to reshape the prominent Washington landmark. The ruling questions whether the board had the statutory power to make such significant changes to the facility without additional oversight or approval.

The two-week timeline for compliance means the president must act quickly to remove existing signage and branding bearing his name. The order does not address whether Trump can appeal the decision or seek to modify the renovation plans in other ways.

The Kennedy Center board has not publicly commented on how it will implement the court's directive or what impact the ruling will have on any other planned changes to the facility.

cards.headline: U.S. Southern Command meets with Cuban military officials
cards.teaser: The head of U.S. Southern Command met with Cuban military leaders near Guantanamo Bay as tensions between the two governments escalate.
cards.body:
Gen. Francis L. Donovan, commander of U.S. Southern Command, met with senior Cuban military officials on Friday near Naval Station Guantanamo Bay. The meeting included Cuba's First Deputy Minister of the Chief of the General Staff Roberto Legra Sotolongo and other military leaders.

The talks occurred as the Trump administration increased pressure on Cuba. Southern Command announced the meeting after it concluded on Friday.

cards.headline: Pentagon signs $9 billion contract with Dell amid conflict concerns
cards.teaser: A new Defense Department contract with Dell raises questions after President Trump publicly promoted the company and purchased its stock.
cards.body:
The Department of Defense awarded Dell a $9.7 billion contract over five years to provide Microsoft software and cloud services. The agreement aims to modernize and consolidate the Pentagon's technology systems.

The deal has drawn scrutiny regarding potential conflicts of interest. President Trump previously promoted Dell's products and invested in company stock before the contract was finalized.

cards.headline: Judge reopens Trump's $10 billion IRS lawsuit
cards.teaser: A federal judge agreed to reopen President Trump's suit against the IRS after intervenors challenged a settlement creating an anti-weaponization fund.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Florida has agreed to reopen President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS. The decision came after intervenors challenged a settlement agreement between the Department of Justice and Trump that would have dismissed the case.

Under the previous agreement, both parties had consented to voluntarily dismiss the suit in exchange for establishing an "anti-weaponization" fund. The judge sided with those who argued this settlement tainted the case, allowing it to move forward for additional examination.

cards.headline: New Jersey detention facility becomes test for DHS Secretary Mullin
cards.teaser: Protesters and detainees clash over conditions at Delaney Hall as the facility presents the first major challenge for the new Homeland Security chief.
cards.body:
The Delaney Hall Facility in Newark, New Jersey has become a flashpoint in disputes over immigration detention policies. The 1,000-bed private detention center houses detainees who have raised claims of inhumane living conditions and inadequate medical care, while protesters have been arrested outside the facility.

New Jersey's governor and attorney general announced that state police will take over policing functions from federal immigration officers at the site. As part of this transition, state police will establish a "peaceful protected zone" for demonstrators. The announcement comes as federal agents have been reported arriving at the facility in increased numbers.

cards.headline: Trump endorses Pam Evette for South Carolina governor over Rep. Mace
cards.teaser: President Trump backed Lt. Gov. Pam Evette in the South Carolina gubernatorial race, snubbing Rep. Nancy Mace who is also running.
cards.body:
President Trump endorsed Lt. Gov. Pam Evette as a Republican challenger to Rep. Nancy Mace's gubernatorial campaign in South Carolina on Friday. In a Truth Social post, Trump called Evette an "America First Patriot" who never wavered in her support.

The endorsement marks a split between Trump and Mace, a sitting Republican congresswoman seeking the governorship. Trump described Evette as a good friend, fighter, and winner in his backing of her candidacy.

cards.headline: Democrat Talarico leads Texas Attorney General Paxton in Senate poll
cards.teaser: State Rep. James Talarico holds a 3-point advantage over Ken Paxton in a post-runoff poll of likely Texas voters.
cards.body:
A poll released Friday by Texas Public Opinion Research shows state Rep. James Talarico leading in the Texas Senate race. Forty-seven percent of likely general election voters backed Talarico, compared with 44 percent for Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton.

The survey was conducted after the primary runoffs concluded. Talarico, the Democratic candidate, holds a three-point advantage over his Republican opponent heading into the general election.
